diagram_name: Traditional Health Knowledge Around the World
learning_objective: Students describe how different cultures and communities use traditional knowledge to protect the body from the environment, comparing practices across regions.
specification:
Type: map **sim-id:** traditional-health-knowledge-map
**Library:** Leaflet
**Status:** Specified Bloom Taxonomy: Understand (L2) Bloom Taxonomy Verb: describe, explain, compare Learning objective: Students describe how different cultures and communities use traditional knowledge to protect the body from the environment, comparing practices across regions. Geographic scope: World map with five highlighted regions Locations and markers: - West Africa: icon of a woven wide-brimmed hat — "Woven hats and light cotton clothing protect from strong sun." - Arctic (Inuit communities): icon of layered fur clothing — "Layered animal-skin clothing traps warm air against the body in extreme cold." - Latin America / Mediterranean: icon of a teacup — "Herbal teas like mint, chamomile, and ginger soothe upset stomachs and help the body rest." - East Asia: icon of a soup bowl — "Warm soups and rest support the body's healing during cold weather." - South Asia: icon of a glass of milk — "Turmeric milk is a traditional comfort remedy for minor coughs and colds." Legend: Each marker icon matches a category — clothing, food/drink — shown in a small key in the corner Interactive features: - Click a region marker to open an infobox with the practice name, a description, and what part of the environment it protects against (sun, cold, upset stomach, general wellness) - Hover a marker for a one-line preview before clicking - A "Compare Two Regions" button lets a student pick two markers and see their infoboxes side by side Color scheme: Warm gold for sun/heat protection, cool blue for cold protection, green for food/drink remedies Implementation: Leaflet map with custom marker icons and popups; teacher-facing tool for read-aloud exploration, since Grade 3 students are still developing independent reading fluency
